prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original fan-made production sprite sheet for a side-view tactical video game, faithful to Metal Gear Solid V The Phantom Pain (1984). EXACTLY 4 columns by 4 rows, exactly 16 independently DRAWN full-body poses of ONE same character. Pure flat magenta #FF00FF canvas with five thin continuous pure cyan #00FFFF vertical grid lines and five horizontal grid lines, including outer boundaries. Each equal square cell must contain exactly one complete character, wholly inside, generous empty margin at least 30 pixels, no extremity or equipment on guides. Fixed camera, strict orthographic RIGHT-facing profile, feet bottom aligned, identical physical scale every frame. Detailed crisp military pixel art, clear small-scale silhouette, no scenery, no ground shadow, no text, no labels, no logos, no watermark. The sixteen poses must be genuinely different drawings, never simple shifted duplicates. Four phases per row in left-to-right time order, preserve all costume and identity features in EVERY pose. Keep weapons and hands compact inside their cell. Subject: Code Talker in MGSV The Phantom Pain 1984. Extremely elderly Navajo man with very deeply wrinkled long face, sparse shoulder-length white hair and almost bald crown, pale cloudy eyes. White collared shirt, dark waistcoat, bolo tie with small turquoise stone. Dark brown wool blanket over shoulders and knees. Seated in his recognizable simple dark-frame MANUAL WHEELCHAIR: brown backrest, two large rear spoked wheels, two small front caster wheels, footrests supporting dark-trousered legs and brown soft shoes. Faithful to official Konami TPP face portrait and Shinkawa concept of Code Talker in wheelchair. This sheet depicts wheelchair mobility, NOT him running or fighting. One complete seated man and chair per cell, strict RIGHT-facing side-view. Row1 four seated breathing/idle stages, slight fingers/head changes. Row2 four rightward wheelchair movement stages: hands grasp wheel rim, push halfway, release, return hands; distinct wheel-spoke phase and elbow placement, no body teleport. Row3 four restrained conversation/inspection hand gestures, lifting hand, indicating ahead, lowering, hand on blanket. Row4 four subtle hunching then recovering seated poses. Preserve blanket, full chair wheels and footrests every frame. No cigars smoke or external marks, no gun, no standing up, no generic feather headdress or stereotypes.

references.kind: secondary mirror of attributed Konami/Shinkawa concept and game model

notes: Complete authored poses, right-facing readable identity and distinctive mobility/costume maintained.
Code Talker uses seated wheelchair motion; Huey uses both external leg braces; Eli retains child proportions as applicable.
Pixel-art adaptation and four-frame archive clips; not a claim of exact 1:1 likeness or complete combat implementation.
